sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 27.12.2018, passed by the tribunal, in MVC No.344/2018, seeking enhancement of compensation.
Heard the arguments and perused the records.
3. In this case, the factum of accident, death of deceased in the said accident and coverage of insurance are not in dispute.

4. In the present case the tribunal has held income of Rs.9,000/- per month and applying the multiplier of 7 as the deceased was aged 65 years old and by deducting 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses, awarded the compensation, which is found to be on lesser side.
Therefore, the same is required to be enhanced.
5. The deceased was aged 65 years old and that the accident occurred on 13.01.2018.

For the accident year 2018, in the absence of proof of income, notional income is to be taken as Rs.11,750/-,
as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The appropriate applicable multiplier is 7.

Even though two claimants are married daughters and others are wife and major children, all are doing agricultural work in the village where even NC: 2023:KHC-D:10713 though the daughters are married and residing along with their husband respectively, but dependency is to be considered as they are mutually dependent on each other.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Birender and others, reported in AIR 2020 SC 434 has decided

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Birender and others, reported in AIR 2020 SC 434
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the major children are also entitled for compensation under the head loss of dependency
. Therefore considering the size of the family, 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.

Therefore, loss of dependency is reassessed and quantified as Rs.7,40,250/- (Rs.11,750 minus 1/4th x 12 x 7).
6.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782 and in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head 'loss of NC: 2023:KHC-D:10713 consortium', along with 10% escalation.

7. Further, a compensation of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded under the head 'loss of estate' and 'funeral and transportation' respectively, along with 10% escalation.
Therefore under these heads Rs.33,000/- (Rs.15,000 x 2 + 10%) is awarded.

8. Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads.

9. Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.9,93,250/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.5,74,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
The insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

10. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 27.12.2018, passed by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Haveri, in MVC No.344/2018 stands modified.
iii) The claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,93,250/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10713 iv) The claimants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 75 days in filing the appeal.
v) The insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
vi) Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of this judgment.
vii) No order as to costs.
viii) Draw award accordingly.
